findings.text: build_worklist() is called with no arguments, so include_parentless stays False and the shared-physical_base families the plan names as half of this detection are unreachable from the command line. The renderer already carries the fallback for them (parent = family.get('parent') or family.get('physical_base'), line 5972), a branch --target groups can never enter; either pass include_parentless=True or drop the dead fallback and say the target is the parented axis only.

The groups branch returns before any other option is consumed, so --ids, --physics-domain, --unreviewed, --report-only, -c and --force are accepted and silently ignored: `sn review --target groups --physics-domain magnetics` reports the whole catalog while reading as a scoped run. A click.UsageError on the combination (or a line in the option help) is the cheap fix; silently discarding a user-supplied filter is the shape this project fails closed against.

_FAMILY_QUERY_MARKER couples the stub to a literal substring of harmonize's Cypher. The direction is safe — a rewritten query returns [] and both cases fail on `assert len(_worklist_from_output(...)) > 0` rather than passing on an empty worklist — but the marker will have to be re-derived by whoever next edits that query. A note in the docstring naming the invariant would spare them the search.

justifications.durability: The delivered behaviour is real rather than asserted: an independent re-run from an archive of the implementation commit gives 2 passed, and the guard fires under a mutation I wrote myself. The test's coupling to harmonize's query text fails loudly rather than quietly, which is the right direction. Two costs: merging this node's three commits onto current main is not clean — git merge-tree --write-tree reports conflicted stage entries for both docs/plans/sn-catalog-audit-instrument.html and docs/evidence/archive/sn-catalog-audit-instrument-landed.html, because main advanced past the node's base while it ran and the plan-version line is exactly where that conflict concentrates, so the landing needs a manual resolution. And returning before the batching, concurrency and reviewer-profile machinery means the grouped target shares none of what the plan's own decision rationale named as the reason to prefer a flag over a separate command; that is a defensible read of read-only, but it is a divergence from the stated rationale and belongs in the record.
justifications.evidence: The declared clause is met literally: one case patches GraphClient with a stub that serves only the family query and asserts the four fields reach both the JSON and the rendered line; the second patches mark_members_for_regen, stamp_harmonized, mark_families_for_regen and restamp_harmonized_families to raise, calls each directly to show the ban is live, and requires the command to succeed. The patch point is at the GraphClient boundary rather than on build_worklist, so the four fields are produced by real code, which I confirmed by reading _resolve_gc (harmonize.py:214) — its function-local import is what makes the module-attribute patch effective, and sn.py holds no module-level binding of the four names (only line 2735, inside a different command). The negative control's first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim and the run reddens on the recorded AssertionError. I reproduced both directions from a git archive of 04b0794b4 on a debug partition: 2 passed unmutated, and my own mutation reddened the ban case with AssertionError('grouped review must not mutate the graph'). Not full marks because the recorded '2 failed' rests on two different failures: the fields case reddened with TypeError('missing 1 required positional argument'), not with the ban, so only the ban case actually demonstrates the refusal — a mutation passing a real parent list would have been the sharper control.
justifications.fit: Naming and prose are by mechanism throughout: _report_drifting_families, no plan, sprint or ticket identifiers in symbols, filenames or comments, and no AI attribution. The commit subjects are conventional and both carry bodies that state why — the cohort defects per-identity review cannot see. The docstring on the reporter names the reason the read-only decision exists, and the function-local import that makes the ban patch effective is the sort of thing this codebase wants. The figure is an SVG in the fenced figures directory, embedded with the project-absolute src /imas-codex/figures/... in the evidence record, whose anchor the plan section links; the plan section itself carries no figure, which is fine for a single landing. The help text for --target states the target reports the worklist and writes nothing, which is accurate for the call as made.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The goal — a grouped review target that reports drifting name families from the existing harmonize surface without mutating the graph — is delivered and I verified each half. `--target groups` is a third value of the Choice, the branch imports build_worklist and nothing else from harmonize, and it returns before reviewer resolution, audit and state construction, so the target reaches no model and spends nothing. The rendering and JSON worklist both carry parent, member count, drift and anchor, which are build_worklist's own keys (harmonize.py:443-490). Two gaps keep it below full: build_worklist() is called with defaults so the shared-physical_base bucket is unreachable though the renderer handles it, and the scoping options are silently discarded rather than refused.
justifications.scope_discipline: Three commits touch exactly the five fenced paths and nothing else. The plan-version meta line moves 32 to 33 in the docs commit, which the dispatch forbids the worker to hand-edit, but reckon owns that line — its own tool text is 'never set plan-version yourself', and _plan_html.py:891 writes it from state — so it is the sanctioned edit path's write, not an authored one, and the manifest says as much. The same commit re-serializes one peer comment body (' to '), a rendering-equivalent normalization from the same writer. The worker did not close its own node: f-scai-groups-wiring is still data-status="open" in the landed plan.
